title: MSA/DPA execution and billing edge-cases kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align on final MSA/DPA redlines, billing edge cases (PO vs invoice, partial month proration), SLA tie-ins, and KMS/SSO requirements for Redwood Private. Action items include security docs, final price worksheet, and draft signature timeline.
topics: DPA jurisdiction and data residency carve-outs
Billing: PO vs invoicing, proration, and taxation
Private deployment KMS/HSM and audit logs
action_items: Jordan Blake: Share redlined MSA PDF by 2026-11-25
Maya Chen: Provide architecture note for Private deployment KMS options by 2026-11-27
Liam O'Connor: Provide list of required DPA amendments by 2026-11-30
Sara Kim: Send sample PO process and billing contact info by 2026-11-24
next_steps: Redwood to share final pricing worksheet and PO/invoice flow
Customer legal to send consolidated redlines to Jordan
Schedule exec signature call week of 2026-11-30 if redlines are agreed
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-23 08:00 PST | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE); Maya Chen (Redwood SE); Avery Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Hightide Head of Procurement); Liam O'Connor (Hightide Legal); Diego Ramos (Hightide CTO); Sara Kim (Finance Manager)

[00:00] Jordan: All right, uh, good morning everyone thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the account exec working with Hightide, um today it's really just a kickoff to close out the MSA and DPA stuff and the billing edge cases Sara flagged. Maya and Avery are with me for technical and onboarding specifics.

[00:18] Priya: Morning. Thanks Jordan. We've got legal and finance on too so we want to make sure we get the path to signature, and avoid the usual back-and-forth.

[00:28] Liam: Yeah hi everyone, Liam here. We'll try to keep the redline list concise but a few items are non-negotiable for us around indemnity and EU data residency carve-outs in the DPA.

[00:41] Diego: And from infra side we need clarity on the KMS options for your Private deployment — we need HSM support and a key rotation cadence that's auditable. Also curious about what log retention you provide for audit.

[00:56] Maya: Totally. We have two KMS options for Private: customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS plus a hardware-backed HSM integration for on-prem scenarios. Audit logs are shipped to your SIEM or retained in the control plane depending on config; retention windows are configurable. I'll drop the architecture note after this call.

[01:12] Sara: Great. On billing, we have a PO process. We prefer monthly invoicing with PO references; however we also need proration rules documented — when a pilot converts mid-month how is that charged? And tax handling across states.

[01:29] Jordan: Understood. We usually support PO-based billing and can itemize usage. For proration we can prorate the seat or capacity commit based on activation date; Maya can explain exact token-level proration patterns. For taxes, our billing team includes a tax section on the invoice but customer-side tax treatment varies, so we'll note that.

[01:46] Priya: On the MSA itself, we have two sticking points: liability caps in section 9 and the termination for convenience notice period. We'd like a 60 day termination for convenience to align with vendor policy.

[01:58] Jordan: Okay. Our standard is 30 days but we can discuss. Can you share the procurement policy wording? Sometimes we can mirror similar commercial customers with slightly higher notice but might need to adjust pricing for longer notice.

[02:12] Priya: I'll share the policy after this meeting.

[02:18] Liam: On the DPA, jurisdiction is key. Hightide processes EU personal data via our EU entity; we need explicit data residency guarantees and sub-processor list. Also, do you support SCCs or equivalent?

[02:30] Maya: We support SCCs and have an EU data residency option on Private and Dedicated tiers. For Hosted we have contractual safeguards and SCCs where applicable, but for strict residency we recommend Private deployment. Note: sometimes the transcript may say 'S C C s' we mean standard EU SCCs.

[02:48] Diego: For latency reasons some of our models need to stay in eu-central region, so the routing policies are relevant — is there guaranteed regional routing?

[02:57] Jordan: Yes, we can configure region pinning for model endpoints. For Dedicated and Private it's straightforward. For Hosted we have regional endpoints but less strict guarantees unless under SLA.

[03:12] Priya: SLA — we reviewed your standard uptime and credits. Can you explain what 'service credit' entails and how it's applied to invoices? Also what is the response SLA for security incidents?

[03:23] Avery: Yes — credits are usually a percentage of monthly service fees applied to the next invoice; the SLA table shows thresholds. For security incidents we have an incident response SLA with defined severity levels — P1 is 1 hour initial response, escalation paths to SRE and CISO as needed. For customers requiring tighter timelines we can adjust under Enterprise SLAs.

[03:46] Liam: We will want the incident response escalation included as a schedule in the MSA or as an addendum, including notification windows.

[03:55] Jordan: We can add a security addendum with those details. I'll coordinate with product/security to insert the schedule.

[04:03] Sara: Back to billing: what about partial month credits if service is down more than X percent? Is that an automatic credit or do we need to claim it?

[04:12] Jordan: Typically credits are applied automatically based on monitored uptime, but some customers prefer claim-based processes. We can agree in the MSA whether it's automatic.

[04:22] Priya: Good. On the DPA data deletion rights: we need confirmation that upon contract termination, customer data will be deleted within 30 days and we require a certificate of deletion.

[04:33] Maya: That is standard for our Private and Dedicated offerings; for Hosted, we support deletion but some backups might be retained for a short retention window for disaster recovery — we can provide an SLA for deletion and certify it. I'll capture exact wording for the DPA changes.

[04:49] Diego: Another infra question — KV cache and session lifetimes. If we do a model upgrade mid-session, is there cache invalidation behavior? We've had issues with stale KV cache in other vendors.

[05:00] Maya: Good question. Our runtime manages KV cache per model version; when you pin versions there won't be silent changes. If you upgrade, the cache is invalidated gracefully; we also support sticky routing to ensure session continuity. Note, sometimes the notes spell KV as 'K V' in transcripts.

[05:19] Liam: Can we get a sample SAML metadata file for your SSO? We need to run it through our IdP team. Also RBAC mapping — we need to map Hightide AD groups to Redwood roles.

[05:29] Jordan: We'll provide SAML metadata and a role-mapping template. Avery will follow up with an RBAC mapping spreadsheet.

[05:39] Avery: Yep I'll send the template. Also, for onboarding timeline — typical pilot is 4 weeks, production roll to be negotiated. If legal is the gating factor, we'll coordinate parallel technical onboarding to cut time.

[05:52] Priya: Our procurement window for new vendors is usually 2–3 weeks after legal sign-off, but finance needs to reconcile PO timing.

[06:02] Sara: We also have a special tax clause for cross-state services; can Redwood accept a tax-exempt designation on the invoice? We can provide exemption certificates.

[06:11] Jordan: Yes, we can accept exemption certificates. We'll need to run that through billing ops — please send example certificates.

[06:20] Liam: There are a couple DPA redlines: one is sub-processor notification timing (we want 30 days) and a right to audit clause. Can you accommodate?

[06:29] Maya: Sub-processor notice is something we push 30 days for major changes. Right to audit is limited; we offer audit reports and SOC2 reports and can negotiate on-site audits in Private deployments under strict controls.

[06:46] Priya: If SOC2 and third-party audits suffice we may avoid an on-site audit. Please send latest SOC2 report and a summary of controls.

[06:55] Jordan: We'll share SOC2 attestation and a security deck.

[07:02] Diego: For Private deployment license fees — are they monthly or annual? And do you support burst capacity?

[07:11] Jordan: Pricing for Private can be structured as monthly reserved capacity or annual commit. Burst capacity is supported as configurable buffer; we can show pricing scenarios in the worksheet.

[07:22] Priya: We'll need a pricing worksheet that shows: base reserved, burst add-ons, and migration costs. Also show the pricing impact of longer MSA notice periods.

[07:34] Jordan: Will do. I'll include scenarios with 30 and 60 day termination clauses.

[07:40] Sara: Another billing edge case — if we run a pilot and usage spikes above expected, can we have an overage cap or notify thresholds so we can opt-in to extra capacity?

[07:50] Avery: Yes threshold alerts and caps are available. You can set hard caps to block overage or soft caps to alert and require approval. We'll include that in the onboarding doc.

[08:02] Liam: On indemnity/loss caps: we'd like to align to industry standards — mutual indemnity for IP and data breaches. Can you accept a liability cap of two times fees or $5M?

[08:16] Jordan: Our default is one times fees; for enterprise deals we can negotiate to two times or a specific figure depending on risk and pricing. We'll flag that to legal.

[08:27] Priya: Given we're regulated, compliance is priority. If we move to Private deployment the security bars are much easier to meet. Is there a preferred timeline to get an on-prem package installed? We might be looking at December for pilot.

[08:38] Maya: For on-prem Private we usually need 6–8 weeks for provisioning and validation, shorter if we reuse existing infra configurations. For a December pilot that might be tight but we can try to accelerate parts in parallel — legal sign-off and initial network prep can happen while infra starts provisioning.

[08:56] Diego: What about routing/egress IPs for firewall rules? We need a fixed egress IP list to allow connections.

[09:04] Maya: We'll provide an IP allowlist and range. For Dedicated/Private we can also do peering or direct connect to avoid dynamic egress ranges.

[09:15] Jordan: OK let's do a quick recap and owners: Jordan will send the redlined MSA template and pricing worksheet; Maya will send KMS/HSM architecture note, SOC2, and SAML metadata; Avery will send RBAC template and onboarding playbook; Priya/Liam will consolidate legal and DPA redlines and Sara will share PO and tax docs.

[09:34] Priya: That sounds good. One question — do you have a standard countersignature flow? We prefer DocuSign execution and countersignature within five business days.

[09:44] Jordan: DocuSign is fine. We aim for countersign within five business days; actual time depends on final redlines.

[09:51] Liam: If we see any non-starters in the MSA, we'll call them out in the consolidated redline doc.

[09:57] Jordan: Perfect. Anything else?

[10:00] Sara: No, that's all from finance.

[10:03] Diego: Nothing further.

[10:05] Priya: Great thanks everyone.

[10:08] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. I'll put the timeline in the calendar and propose the exec signature slot week of 2026-11-30.

[10:15] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'sam-el' for SAML), and some speaker labels may be generic; redline items were called out explicitly for legal to send.
